messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [REDACTED]
Gender: Male
Age: 61 years old
Admission Date: [REDACTED]
Discharge Date: [REDACTED]
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course Summary:

The patient was admitted to the hospital on [REDACTED] with progressively worsening shortness of breath, weakness and fatigue. The patient was diagnosed with aortic valve stenosis, hypertensive heart disease, coronary artery disease, and COPD.

During the course of the hospital stay, various tests were performed including cardiac catheterization and transthoracic echocardiography. These tests showed significant stenosis of the proximal and mid-left anterior descending artery, severe aortic valve stenosis with moderate insufficiency, an ejection fraction of 32%, and significant atherosclerotic burden in the ascending and descending aortas and aortic arch.

Based on the results of the tests, the patient underwent minimally invasive aortic valve replacement with a 27 mm·St. Jude Trifecta stented pericardial bioprosthesis under general endotracheal anesthesia. Standard monitors were used including cerebral oximetry. The procedure was completed without any complications. The postoperative TEE showed that the previously described aortic arch atheroma remained intact.

Following the procedure, the patient was monitored closely and his condition gradually improved. The patient did not experience any perioperative stroke events or other complications. The patient was discharged home in a stable condition five days postoperatively.

Upon discharge, the patient was advised to continue taking his medications for hypertension and high cholesterol as prescribed by his doctor. The patient was also advised to avoid smoking and other forms of substance abuse, and to follow a healthy diet and exercise regime. The patient was advised to follow up with his physician as recommended.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
1. The condition chiefly responsible for the admission is severe aortic valve stenosis with moderate insufficiency, which caused his worsening breathlessness and was treated with aortic valve replacement.
2. It belongs to chapter I (diseases of the circulatory system).
3. Isolated aortic valve disease with no stated rheumatic cause is classed as nonrheumatic, so the category is I35.

CODE: I35
